Hi Christian,

Sarah passed this to me, I am Hal, the technical side of HeliumDeploy. Sorry the delivery was handled that way. Let us find out what the Thor P2 is actually doing, because a drop onto concrete usually knocks something loose rather than killing the unit, and I would like to know which before anything else.

First, before powering it on, look it over. Check that the case is not cracked or bowed, that the fan still spins freely by hand with no rubbing, and that the heatsink on the board is sitting flat and firm. On a dropped unit a heatsink that has shifted or a connector that has popped half out is the most common finding. If anything smells burnt or scorched, stop there, leave it unplugged and tell me.

Then power it up with the supplied power supply only, and watch the first thirty seconds. Tell me whether the fan spins, whether the screen lights up, and exactly what the screen shows, word for word or as a photo. Plug it into your router with the ethernet cable and check that the two small lights at the port come on. The T. P2 takes a DHCP address, so you can find it in your router's client list, then type that IP into a browser on the same network to reach the web UI.

Once the UI opens, two things matter. The pool page needs the stratum URL and port, your worker name and a password of x, and if any one of those is wrong the unit runs but reports nothing, which looks exactly like "not hashing". Tell me the pool URL, the port and the worker name you entered, and I will check them. The dashboard also shows the chip count and the local hashrate. Two BM1373 chips should be detected and the figure should settle near 10 TH/s over fifteen to thirty minutes, since a short sample swings wildly. If it shows zero chips, or only one, that is a board-level finding and I need to know it.

So that I can settle this in one go, please reply with a short video of it powering up with the screen visible, a clear photo of the serial label on the unit and of any visible damage to the case, fan or heatsink, the firmware version shown in the web UI, and the pool details above. With that I can tell you straight away whether this is a settings fix, a firmware fix, a part, or damage that happened in that drop, and I will take it from there.

If you want a faster back and forth, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can tag @nullhashrate, our hardware lead, who is very active there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
